headline: FBI ties $6.3B Binance heist to North Korea; trojanized Claude Code extension and Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days stay active

bullets.text: New since the last SITREP: SecurityWeek reports a malicious Claude Code extension served in a Cursor supply chain attack, now 7 outlets. BleepingComputer says it planted SSH backdoors; WIRED says malicious Claude extensions reached thousands of devices.

Binance, 8 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers. The Record names TraderTraitor and says the FBI urges the crypto industry to block transactions; SecurityWeek says it flagged over 600 addresses.

Ivanti patched two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of today, 2026-11-02, and 2026-11-13.

Chainalysis disclosed a breach it attributes to "offensive agentic techniques", Help Net Security reports. The Hacker News says the intrusion reached internal tools and exposed customer identity data.
Polymarket returned $3.9 million to traders, and DebugBear cites a DNS hijack, SecurityWeek reports. The Hacker News earlier described about $2.7 million stolen through a hijacked DebugBear script.
CISA KEV due dates for the max-severity GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 and the Cisco ASA/FTD flaw CVE-2026-76418 passed on 2026-11-01. Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab after an attempted RCE attack.

actions: If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches today, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
If you handle crypto transactions, screen against the addresses the FBI flagged for the Binance heist, and warn staff about Binance-themed scams.
If GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) or Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) are still unpatched, patch now; both KEV due dates have passed.
Find any LXD and MicroCloud deployments, check the vendor advisory for the CVSS 10.0 flaw, and patch them.
If your sites load the DebugBear script, review it against DebugBear's DNS hijack statement and check for injected code.
